messages.content: I want an API that takes an IP address and returns company data with contact information if available.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data. This function is commonly used for API calls and web scraping. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for two of the most popular “IP → Company” APIs that actually expose contact details (phone, email, logo, etc.).  
Both services offer a free tier, a generous set of fields, and a simple JSON output that you can consume in any language.

| Service | Free Tier | Typical Rate Limit | Contact Fields Returned | Example Endpoint |
|---------|-----------|--------------------|------------------------|------------------|
| **ipstack** | 10 000 requests/month | 10 000 reqs/mo (free) | `company.name`, `company.domain`, `company.phone`, `company.email`, `company.logo_url` | `http://api.ipstack.com/<IP>?access_key=<KEY>&fields=ip,continent_code,country_code,region_name,city,zip,latitude,longitude,timezone,isp,domain,as,as_name,company.*` |
| **ipgeolocation.io** | 1 000 requests/day | 1 000 reqs/day (free) | `company.name`, `company.website`, `company.phone`, `company.email`, `company.logo_url` | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=<KEY>&ip=<IP>` |

> ⚠️ **Privacy note** – These APIs return *public* data only. No personal data is exposed beyond what is publicly listed on the Internet (e.g., WHOIS records). Always respect the terms of service and local regulations when storing or displaying this data.

---

## 1️⃣ ipstack

### Sign‑up & Get Your Key
1. Go to <https://ipstack.com/> and register for a free account.  
2. In the dashboard you’ll find your **Access Key**.

### Request Format
```text
GET http://api.ipstack.com/<IP_ADDRESS>?access_key=<YOUR_ACCESS_KEY>&fields=ip,continent_code,country_code,region_name,city,zip,latitude,longitude,timezone,isp,domain,as,as_name,company.*
```

### Sample Response (JSON)
```json
{
  "ip": "134.201.250.155",
  "continent_code": "NA",
  "country_code": "US",
  "region_name": "California",
  "city": "Los Angeles",
  "zip": "90012",
  "latitude": 34.0459,
  "longitude": -118.2477,
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "isp": "AT&T Services, Inc.",
  "domain": "att.net",
  "as": "AS7018 AT&T Services, Inc.",
  "as_name": "AT&T Services, Inc.",
  "company": {
    "name": "AT&T Services, Inc.",
    "domain": "att.com",
    "phone": "+1-800-331-0500",
    "email": "support@att.com",
    "logo_url": "https://cdn.ipstack.com/company_logos/att.png"
  }
}
```

> 👉 **Tip** – The `fields=` query param lets you cherry‑pick exactly what you need, keeping payload size small.

### Quick Python Example
```python
import requests

def get_ip_info(ip, api_key):
    url = f"http://api.ipstack.com/{ip}"
    params = {
        "access_key": api_key,
        "fields": "ip,continent_code,country_code,region_name,city,zip,latitude,longitude,timezone,isp,domain,as,as_name,company.*"
    }
    resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    API_KEY = "YOUR_IPSTACK_KEY"
    print(get_ip_info("134.201.250.155", API_KEY))
```

---

1. Register at <https://ipgeolocation.io/>.  
2. Grab your **API Key** from the dashboard.

```text
GET https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=<YOUR_API_KEY>&ip=<IP_ADDRESS>
```

### Quick Python Example
```python
import requests

def get_company_from_ip(ip, api_key):
    url = "https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo"
    params = {"apiKey": api_key, "ip": ip}
    resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    data = resp.json()
    # Pull out the company block
    return data.get("company", {})

if __name__ == "__main__":
    API_KEY = "YOUR_IPGEOLOCATION_KEY"
    print(get_company_from_ip("134.201.250.155", API_KEY))
```
